title: Monomial ideal Tor-one tests imply acyclicity for cancellative monomial modules
statement: Let $Q$ be a commutative monoid, written additively, let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $h:Q\hookrightarrow G$ be an injective monoid homomorphism. Set $D=\mathbf Z[Q]$, the ring with abelian-group basis $z^q$ for $q\in Q$ and multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. Let $M$ be a $D$-module. A monoid ideal $I\subseteq Q$ means $I+Q\subseteq I$, including the empty ideal; let $\mathbf Z[I]\subseteq D$ be its monomial span. Assume that $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(M,D/\mathbf Z[I])=0$ for every such $I$. Let $U\subseteq T\subseteq G$ be subsets with $T+h(Q)\subseteq T$ and $U+h(Q)\subseteq U$. Write $\mathbf Z[T]$ and $\mathbf Z[U]$ for the free abelian groups on their indicated sets, made $D$-modules by $z^q[t]=[t+h(q)]$, and put $V=\mathbf Z[T]/\mathbf Z[U]$. Then $\operatorname{Tor}^D_i(M,V)=0$ for every $i>0$. All Tor groups are the projective-resolution functors [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Empty $U$, empty $T$, and $U=T$ are allowed.

source.place: Agent algebra lemma for ILO Expose X 1.3(vii) and Lemma 1.5; dimension shifting and monomial filtrations using Tag 00M0 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor) and Tag 0BNF (lemma-tor-commutes-filtered-colimits). Neither Stacks lemma alone states this criterion.

proof.text: Keep $Q,G,h,D$ fixed. For a $D$-module $N$, write $A(N)$ for the condition $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,D/\mathbf Z[I])=0$ for every monoid ideal $I\subseteq Q$. We first prove the degree-one conclusion for every $N$ satisfying $A(N)$, not just for $M$. Choose a projective resolution $P_\bullet\to N$ as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For any $D$-module $W$, regard $P_\bullet\otimes_D W$ as a cochain complex $C(W)$ by putting $C(W)^{-j}=P_j\otimes_DW$ for $j\ge0$ and $C(W)^j=0$ for $j>0$. Thus $H^{-1}(C(W))=\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,W)$ and $C(0)=0$.

source.place: Tag 00LY (section-tor), projective-resolution definition; agent notation for the simultaneous degree-one argument.

proof.text: If $0\to W_1\to W_2\to W_3\to0$ is short exact, each $P_j$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] makes $0\to C(W_1)\to C(W_2)\to C(W_3)\to0$ degreewise short exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] in degree $-1$. It gives exactness of $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,W_1)\to\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,W_2)\to\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,W_3)$. Therefore vanishing of the two outer groups implies vanishing of the middle group. This uses the full homology sequence, including its term before the middle Tor group.

source.place: Tag 00M0 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor), proof via Homology Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain); tensor exactness Tag 00HD (lemma-flat).

proof.text: For a small directed system $(W_a)$, [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits], with the tensor flip $p\otimes w\mapsto w\otimes p$, identifies $C(\varinjlim_aW_a)$ with the termwise colimit of $C(W_a)$. Filtered module colimits are computed on abelian groups: the rule $d[w_a]=[dw_a]$ defines their $D$-action and verifies the module colimit universal property. Put $Z_a=\ker(C(W_a)^{-1}\to C(W_a)^0)$ and $B_a=\operatorname{im}(C(W_a)^{-2}\to C(W_a)^{-1})$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] to $0\to Z_a\to C(W_a)^{-1}\to C(W_a)^0$ and to $C(W_a)^{-2}\to B_a\to0$ and $0\to B_a\to C(W_a)^{-1}$. It identifies their colimits with the kernel and image in the colimit complex. Applying it once more to $0\to B_a\to Z_a\to H^{-1}(C(W_a))\to0$ gives $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,\varinjlim_aW_a)\cong\varinjlim_a\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,W_a)$. In particular, a directed colimit of degree-one-acyclic modules is degree-one-acyclic.

source.place: Tag 0BNF (lemma-tor-commutes-filtered-colimits), proof; Tags 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits) and 00DB (lemma-directed-colimit-exact). Argument written for the second variable using its fixed projective-resolution complex.

proof.text: For a finite subset $E\subseteq T\setminus U$, put $T_E=U\cup\bigcup_{t\in E}(t+h(Q))$ and $W_E=\mathbf Z[T_E]/\mathbf Z[U]$. This is the submodule of $V$ spanned over $\mathbf Z$ by $T_E\setminus U$. Enumerate $E=\{t_1,\ldots,t_r\}$, set $T_0=U$ and $T_j=T_{j-1}\cup(t_j+h(Q))$, and put $W_j=\mathbf Z[T_j]/\mathbf Z[U]$. These are stable subsets and $0=W_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq W_r=W_E$. Define $I_j=\{q\in Q:t_j+h(q)\in T_{j-1}\}$. Stability of $T_{j-1}$ gives $I_j+Q\subseteq I_j$. The map $D\to W_j/W_{j-1}$, $z^q\mapsto[t_j+h(q)]$, is onto. Injectivity of $h$ and cancellation in $G$ make the values $t_j+h(q)$ distinct for distinct $q$. Thus the surviving values form an abelian-group basis of the quotient, and its kernel is exactly $\mathbf Z[I_j]$. The displayed map is $D$-linear by the action formula, so $W_j/W_{j-1}\cong D/\mathbf Z[I_j]$. This coefficient-by-coefficient calculation also covers $I_j=\varnothing$ and $I_j=Q$.

source.place: Agent basis calculation supplying the monomial filtration used in the proof of this item; ILO Expose X 1.3(vii), printed p.140, and Lemma 1.5, printed p.142, are its intended application.

proof.text: Assume $A(N)$. For each finite $E$, induct on $j$ in Step 4. The base $W_0=0$ has zero tensor complex. The factor $W_j/W_{j-1}\cong D/\mathbf Z[I_j]$ has zero Tor one by $A(N)$ and functoriality in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Step 2 applied to $0\to W_{j-1}\to W_j\to W_j/W_{j-1}\to0$ gives $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,W_j)=0$. In particular it vanishes on $W_E$. The finite subsets of $T\setminus U$, ordered by inclusion, form a small nonempty directed set (the empty subset is included and union is an upper bound). Their $W_E$ have union $V$, since each element of $V$ has finite support in its abelian-group basis $T\setminus U$. This union is their module colimit: compatible maps define a map on any element by choosing one stage containing its support. Step 3 now gives $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,V)=0$. This establishes the degree-one assertion simultaneously for every $N$ with $A(N)$ and every allowed pair $U\subseteq T$.

source.place: Agent finite-filtration induction and directed-union argument, using Tags 00M0 and 0BNF as established in Steps 2 and 3.

proof.text: Let $N$ satisfy $A(N)$ and let $I\subseteq Q$ be a monoid ideal. The pair $T=h(I)$, $U=\varnothing$ is allowed, and $q\mapsto h(q)$ identifies $\mathbf Z[I]$ with $\mathbf Z[h(I)]$ as a $D$-module: it is a bijection on their specified bases and respects translation. Step 5 yields $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,\mathbf Z[I])=0$. The basis inclusion of $\mathbf Z[I]$ in $D$ gives the short exact sequence $0\to\mathbf Z[I]\to D\to D/\mathbf Z[I]\to0$, whose middle term is free of rank one. Applying [lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shift-natural] with $i=1$ and [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] twice gives $\operatorname{Tor}^D_2(N,D/\mathbf Z[I])\cong\operatorname{Tor}^D_2(D/\mathbf Z[I],N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(\mathbf Z[I],N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(N,\mathbf Z[I])=0$. The same computation applies to the empty and full ideals.

source.place: Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right) and the free-middle-term dimension shift from Tag 00LY (section-tor), as stated in lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shift-natural; agent application to monomial ideals.

proof.text: For any short exact sequence $0\to K\to F\to N\to0$ with $F$ free and $A(N)$, [lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shift-natural] with $i=1$ identifies $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(K,D/\mathbf Z[I])$ with $\operatorname{Tor}^D_2(N,D/\mathbf Z[I])$ for every monoid ideal $I$. Step 6 makes the latter zero, hence $A(K)$ holds. Construct such sequences successively without any finiteness hypothesis: start $K_0=M$, let $F_r=\bigoplus_{x\in K_r}D e_x$, send $e_x\mapsto x$, and let $K_{r+1}$ be its kernel. The map is onto since $x$ is the image of $e_x$, so each $0\to K_{r+1}\to F_r\to K_r\to0$ is short exact with free middle term. The original hypothesis is $A(K_0)$, and induction using the first part of this step proves $A(K_r)$ for every $r\ge0$.

source.place: Free-resolution dimension shifting, Tag 00LY (section-tor); explicit free presentations and induction on the successive kernels.

proof.text: Fix $i>0$ and the given $V$. Repeatedly applying [lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shift-natural] to the free presentations of Step 7 gives $\operatorname{Tor}^D_i(M,V)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(K_{i-1},V)$; for $i=1$ this is the identity. Step 7 gives $A(K_{i-1})$, so Step 5 applied to this module makes the right hand side zero. This proves every positive-degree assertion. If $U=T$ (including $T=\varnothing$), then $V=0$ and the same proof has only zero modules in its finite filtration. Empty $U$ needs no modification. No finite generation, sharpness, torsion-freeness of $G$, or ordinary flatness of $M$ was used.

source.place: Agent conclusion by iterated free-middle-term dimension shifting and the degree-one monomial filtration.
